/projects/trash-collection.title: Trash Collection Robot
/projects/trash-collection.description: A robot designed to collect trash autonomously.
p: A robot designed to collect trash autonomously.

We developed an autonomous trash-collection robot integrating computer vision and motor control. The robot is designed to detect water bottles using a Raspberry-pi controlled machine learning model and pick them up using a motor-controlled arm powered by an Arduino.
Led electronics and power system design and planning, ensuring hardware reliability and seamless integration with firmware.
Established communication between the Raspberry Pi and Arduino Uno, enabling the Pi to handle computer vision and the Uno to control the robot’s movement.

/projects/diy-design.title: DIY Design and Fabrication
p: This class at CMU offered me a deep dive into DIY product design and fabrication processes. I learned the design process through engineering sketches, and I learned various fabrication methods such as laser cutting.

The goal of this project was to design a cup holder designed to be sleek, portable, and lightweight. I designed the cupholder to be made out of a single sheet of acrylic which was then shaped into the holder using a heat gun. The handle was designed in a way which made it possible to carry on a backpack.

The goal of this project was to design a paper container that transforms into another object with a different purpose. Inspired by my interest in rock climbing, I designed a box that transports your climbing chalk to the gym and then transforms into a phone holder to record your climbs. The box was made by laser cutting a piece of matboard and includes removable slots to hold your phone.

/projects/impedance-matcher.title: Automated Impedance Matcher
/projects/impedance-matcher.description: A precision automation tool designed to replace manual tuning in dynamic RF sputtering environments.
p: A precision automation tool designed to replace manual tuning in dynamic RF sputtering environments.

In RF sputtering, the chamber acts as a dynamic load with impedance that fluctuates throughout the process. Traditionally in a Hacker Fab, this requires an operator to stay glued to the machine, manually tuning variable capacitors to minimize reflected power (VSWR). This project automates that manual labor using a Teensy 4.1 microcontroller and a custom T-network. The system intercepting forward and reverse power signals to dynamically drive stepper motors, achieving a stabilized performance of ~1.2 VSWR without human intervention.
Reverse-engineered a COTS SW-112 VSWR meter to automate data acquisition by tapping into internal toroidal sensing lines.
Designed a custom PCB that integrates the Teensy 4.1, active cooling, and dedicated motor drivers to replace manual knob-turning with high-precision digital control.
Developed a buffered sensing pipeline using TLV2372IP op-amps to accurately digitize analog signals from high-impedance lines without causing voltage sag.
Implemented an electro-mechanical interface using 0.9 degree stepper motors, providing the high physical resolution and RF noise resistance required for precise capacitor tuning.
Authored a local GUI for an OLED screen and rotary encoder, allowing the operator to toggle between automated and manual modes while viewing real-time telemetry.

Built an automated RF power tuner for a sputtering chamber using a Teensy 4.1, servo-driven capacitors, and a custom shielded PCB to minimize reflected power and stabilize 95W plasma deposition.

Identified voltage drops in sensitive EV control units and audited 50+ hardware requirements across three EV programs, resolving cross-functional gaps and driving cost optimization for underbody components.
Led weekly lab instruction and mentoring for 100+ students in circuit design and debugging, significantly enhancing engagement and exam performance.
Built and tested aircraft systems over 200+ hours, leading team assembly efforts and ensuring FAA-compliant integration of avionics and airframe components.
